{{Use British English|date=January 2017}}
'''Wilson Sibbett'''  {{postnom|country=GBR|CBE|FRS|FRSE|HonFInstP}} (1948 — 15 October 2024) was a British physicist noted for his work on [[ultrashort pulse laser]]s<ref name="trs">{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/page.asp?id=1555|title=Professor Wilson Sibbett FRS, CBE|publisher=The Royal Society|accessdate=2009-01-25}}</ref> and [[Streak camera]]s. He was the Wardlaw Professor of Physics at [[St Andrews University]].

==Early life and education ==
He was born in [[Portglenone]] in [[County Antrim]], [[Northern Ireland]], in March 1948.<ref name="royalsoced.org.uk">{{cite web|url=https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/220_ScotlandschiefadvisoronscienceappointedbyTheRSE.html|title=The Royal Society of Edinburgh &#124; Scotlands chief advisor on science appointed by The RSE|publisher=royalsoced.org.uk|accessdate=2016-08-16|archive-date=6 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306184912/https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/220_ScotlandschiefadvisoronscienceappointedbyTheRSE.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He studied physics at [[Queen's University, Belfast]], and graduated BSc in 1970, then studying at postgraduate level, gaining a PhD in laser physics in 1973. He began lecturing at [[Imperial College London]] in 1973, rising to reader before moving to [[St Andrews University]] as full professor in 1985. From 1988 he was head of physics and astronomy at the university.

== Works ==
Professor Sibbett led a large research team at the university and supported many students in laser physics research and later in the 2020s collaborated with the optical micro manipulation team led by [[Kishan Dholakia]]. He worked with [[Miles Padgett]] and [[Alan James Duncan]] to create optical instruments to measure the [[Orbital angular momentum of light]].<ref>Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh: obituaries 1999, Alan James Duncan</ref>

He was made a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1997, and awarded the [[Rumford Medal]] in 2000.<ref name="trs"/> The Royal Society of Edinburgh elected him their first chief Advisor on Science.<ref name="royalsoced.org.uk"/>

He was appointed a Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in 2001.

In 1989 he was made a Fellow of [[Royal Society of Edinburgh|The Royal Society of Edinburgh]]. He was vice-president for physical sciences from 2010 to 2013.

In 1998, he was elected a Fellow of the [[Optica (society)|Optical Society]], and in 2011, he received the [[Charles Hard Townes Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wilson Sibbett {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Wilson_Sibbett |access-date=2024-09-23 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>

After retirement, he remained a pioneer of the ultrafast laser research community.

Sibbett died on 15 October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam: Wilson Sibbett, 1948-2024 {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/obituaries/2024/wilson_sibbett/ |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>
